title: Re-stratification Triggers and Graduation Periods by Care Management Tier
content:
Three figures move a Care Management member between tiers: an emergency department visit count over 6 months and an inpatient admission count over 12 months, either of which triggers re-stratification to the next tier, and a run of stable months after which the member graduates.

| Care Management tier | Emergency department visits within 6 months that trigger re-stratification | Inpatient admissions within 12 months that trigger re-stratification | Consecutive stable months to graduation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Healthy Living Support | 3 | 2 | 0 |
| Care Coordination Level 1 | 3 | 2 | 3 |
| Care Coordination Level 2 | 3 | 2 | 3 |
| Maternal Care Management | 2 | 1 | 0 |
| Complex Case Management | 0 | 0 | 6 |
| Health Home Services | 3 | 2 | 6 |
| LTSS Service Coordination | 2 | 1 | 0 |

## Meaning of the figures

- **Emergency department visits within 6 months**: the number of emergency department visits within 6 months at which the member is re-stratified to the next tier. A 0 means the trigger does not apply to the tier.
- **Inpatient admissions within 12 months**: the number of inpatient admissions within 12 months at which the member is re-stratified. A 0 means the trigger does not apply to the tier.
- **Consecutive stable months to graduation**: the number of consecutive months meeting care plan goals, with no emergency department visit and no admission, after which the member graduates. A 0 means graduation does not apply to the tier.

## Reading a row (hypothetical counts)

For Care Coordination Level 1 the triggers are 3 emergency visits and 2 admissions:

| Emergency visits in 6 months | Admissions in 12 months | Trigger count reached |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1 | Neither |
| 3 | 0 | Emergency visit trigger |
| 1 | 2 | Admission trigger |
| 3 | 2 | Both |

For Maternal Care Management the same four rows read against 2 visits and 1 admission, so a member with 2 emergency visits in 6 months has already reached that tier's visit trigger.

For graduation, a Health Home Services member needs 6 consecutive stable months, while a Care Coordination Level 2 member needs 3; a member with 5 consecutive stable months has met the Level 2 figure and not the Health Home Services figure.
